messages:
liam: Hey @people-ops 1 emergency: had to go to urgent care in Lisbon yesterday. Paid out of pocket because clinic wanted upfront. Need to submit for reimbursement but their receipt is just a total in EUR and no CPT codes. How do I file this and what do they need? Also got charged VAT 

ena (People Ops): Sorry you had to deal with that. For reimbursement: insurer typically needs an itemized invoice showing dates of service, CPT/diagnosis codes (or at least procedure descriptions), provider name/NPI (if available), and a line-item cost breakdown. For foreign receipts they also want a clear translation and the currency.

liam: Clinic gave a PDF that is basically: "Consulta, 1 x 85.00 EUR" with provider stamp. No codes.

marta: I had this last summer. My clinic wrote a short breakdown on their letterhead with procedure descriptions and signed it. That worked. Also include a bank receipt for the card charge.

ena (People Ops): Steps: 1) Ask the clinic for an itemized invoice or a short statement on letterhead listing services provided & dates. If they don't use CPT, ask for ICD/description or their local procedure codes. 2) If they refuse, write a terse attestation email to the clinic requesting a "medical itemized invoice for insurance reimbursement" and attach the clinic's original PDF. 3) Convert EUR total to USD using the date-of-service exchange rate (insurer often requires conversion). Keep a screenshot of the exchange rate source. 4) Submit claim via insurer portal with receipts + translation + exchange-rate note. 5) If insurer denies for missing codes, we can help draft an appeal letter and contact the broker.

liam: Any sample text I can send the clinic? They're a small private practice and English is spotty.

ena (People Ops): Yes, copy-paste this in Portuguese (or ask them to fill blanks):

```
Subject: Solicitae7e3o de fatura detalhada para reembolso de seguro

Prezados,
Por favor, poderiam fornecer uma fatura detalhada / declarae7e3o em papel timbrado listando as entradas de servie7o (ex.: consulta, exames, procedimentos), datas e valores correspondentes para a consulta de [data] do paciente [nome]? Este documento e9 necesse1rio para reembolso com o seguro.
Atenciosamente,
[nome]
```

(If you want, DM me the clinic name and I'll paste the Portuguese version.)

liam: Sending that now. Also, how about VAT? Can I claim that back through insurer?

ena (People Ops): Insurer reimbursements usually cover the billed medical amount; VAT treatment varies by insurer & country. Some insurers reimburse inclusive of VAT if it's a medical service. Add the VAT line in the invoice and we'll include it in the claim. If insurer declines VAT, we can show guidance on VAT reclaim options for non-residents separately.

people-ops-bot: Helpful links: Claims portal: https://benefits.example.com/claims, Foreign receipts guide: https://hr.example.com/docs/foreign-receipts, Sample appeal templates: https://hr.example.com/claims/appeals

liam: Clinic replied with a signed note listing: "Consulta 85, ECG 30" but no provider ID. Will that be ok?

ena (People Ops): Good. That should be enough to file. Include clinic contact info and photo of the provider stamp. File claim, attach the note, original PDF, card transaction screenshot, and a short English translation you can paste in the claim form. If insurer asks for provider ID, we'll follow up with the clinic and broker.

marta: Also save any email thread with clinic. Insurers like a clear chain of verification.

liam: Filing now. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:

ena (People Ops): Ping me the claim number once submitted and wee28099ll track. If denied for coding, wee28099ll help escalate via broker.
